The `fbi` package wraps the FBI's Crime Data Explorer (CDE) API
(<https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/>), giving R users direct access to Uniform
Crime Reporting (UCR) and National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS)
data: crime counts and rates, arrests, incident-level NIBRS detail,
Supplemental Homicide Reports (SHR), police employment, and NIBRS
participation.

No API key is required for the current CDE host. (`get_api_key()` and
`set_api_key()` are retained only for backward compatibility with the
package's legacy `api.data.gov`-hosted predecessor and are no-ops today.)

This vignette works through the package's main functions using real example
agencies drawn from several different states, so you can see the shape of
the data at the agency, state, and national level.


``` r
library(fbi)
```

## Lookups

Before requesting crime data you often need to look up a state abbreviation,
a valid offense code, or an agency's ORI (the 9-character identifier the CDE
API uses for law enforcement agencies).


``` r
states <- get_states()
head(states)
#>   stateAbbreviation  stateName
#> 1                AL    Alabama
#> 2                AK     Alaska
#> 3                AZ    Arizona
#> 4                AR   Arkansas
#> 5                CA California
#> 6                CO   Colorado
```


``` r
offenses <- get_offense_codes("crime-trend")
head(offenses)
#>   code              label
#> 1  ASS Aggravated Assault
#> 2  HOM           Homicide
#> 3  RPE               Rape
#> 4  ROB            Robbery
#> 5  ARS              Arson
#> 6  BUR           Burglary
```

`get_offense_codes()` also accepts `"arrest"` and `"hate-crime"` for their
respective offense vocabularies.

`get_agency_info()` looks up agencies by name from the package's bundled
agency table (`fbi_api_agencies`) -- no network call required:


``` r
get_agency_info("Oakland Police Department", state = "california", ori_only = TRUE)
#>                   agency_name       ori
#> 905 Oakland Police Department CA0010900
```

Throughout the rest of this vignette we use six agencies spread across six
states, all validated live against the current API:

| ORI | Agency | State |
|---|---|---|
| `CA0010900` | Oakland Police Department | California |
| `TX0050100` | Archer City Police Department | Texas |
| `NY0112000` | Homer Village Police Department | New York |
| `WA0271300` | Orting Police Department | Washington |
| `FL0010100` | Gainesville Police Department | Florida |
| `MA0092900` | Maynard Police Department | Massachusetts |

## Summarized Crime

`get_agency_crime()`, `get_estimated_crime()`, and `get_estimated_arson()`
wrap the CDE's `summarized/{level}/{offense}` endpoint at the agency, state,
and national level respectively. ("Estimated" here just means state/national
level -- there is no separate estimates endpoint.)


``` r
oakland_crime <- get_agency_crime("CA0010900", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
oakland_crime
#>    geography                              offense  period count   rate
#> 1  CA0010900                California Clearances 01-2019    NA  16.12
#> 2  CA0010900                California Clearances 02-2019    NA  14.63
#> 3  CA0010900                California Clearances 03-2019    NA  16.12
#> 4  CA0010900                  California Offenses 01-2019    NA  34.38
#> 5  CA0010900                  California Offenses 02-2019    NA  30.66
#> 6  CA0010900                  California Offenses 03-2019    NA  35.95
#> 7  CA0010900 Oakland Police Department Clearances 01-2019   106  24.42
#> 8  CA0010900 Oakland Police Department Clearances 02-2019    40   9.22
#> 9  CA0010900 Oakland Police Department Clearances 03-2019    37   8.52
#> 10 CA0010900   Oakland Police Department Offenses 01-2019   472 108.75
#> 11 CA0010900   Oakland Police Department Offenses 02-2019   368  84.79
#> 12 CA0010900   Oakland Police Department Offenses 03-2019   438 100.91
#> 13 CA0010900             United States Clearances 01-2019    NA  12.20
#> 14 CA0010900             United States Clearances 02-2019    NA  10.89
#> 15 CA0010900             United States Clearances 03-2019    NA  12.14
#> 16 CA0010900               United States Offenses 01-2019    NA  27.84
#> 17 CA0010900               United States Offenses 02-2019    NA  24.11
#> 18 CA0010900               United States Offenses 03-2019    NA  27.66
```

Agency- and state-level responses include comparison rows (state and
national rates alongside the agency's own), so a query for one agency
returns more than just that agency's offense categories -- rows for
"California Offenses" or "United States Offenses" carry a real `rate` but no
agency-specific `count`.


``` r
texas_crime <- get_estimated_crime("TX", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
texas_crime
#>    geography                  offense  period count  rate
#> 1         TX         Texas Clearances 01-2019  3425 11.89
#> 2         TX         Texas Clearances 02-2019  3083 10.70
#> 3         TX         Texas Clearances 03-2019  3266 11.33
#> 4         TX           Texas Offenses 01-2019  9688 33.63
#> 5         TX           Texas Offenses 02-2019  8553 29.68
#> 6         TX           Texas Offenses 03-2019  9770 33.90
#> 7         TX United States Clearances 01-2019    NA 12.20
#> 8         TX United States Clearances 02-2019    NA 10.89
#> 9         TX United States Clearances 03-2019    NA 12.14
#> 10        TX   United States Offenses 01-2019    NA 27.84
#> 11        TX   United States Offenses 02-2019    NA 24.11
#> 12        TX   United States Offenses 03-2019    NA 27.66
```


``` r
national_crime <- get_estimated_crime(from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
national_crime
#>   geography                  offense  period count  rate
#> 1        US United States Clearances 01-2019 39196 12.20
#> 2        US United States Clearances 02-2019 34934 10.89
#> 3        US United States Clearances 03-2019 38975 12.14
#> 4        US   United States Offenses 01-2019 89470 27.84
#> 5        US   United States Offenses 02-2019 77385 24.11
#> 6        US   United States Offenses 03-2019 88801 27.66
```


``` r
national_arson <- get_estimated_arson(from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
national_arson
#>   geography                  offense  period count rate
#> 1        US United States Clearances 01-2019   572 0.18
#> 2        US United States Clearances 02-2019   486 0.15
#> 3        US United States Clearances 03-2019   684 0.21
#> 4        US   United States Offenses 01-2019  2598 0.81
#> 5        US   United States Offenses 02-2019  2217 0.69
#> 6        US   United States Offenses 03-2019  2771 0.86
```

## Arrests

`get_arrest_count()` wraps `arrest/{level}/all?type=counts`. With the default
`offense = "all"` it returns a monthly time series; requesting a specific
offense returns a single aggregated total for the whole date range instead,
since the CDE API no longer exposes a per-offense monthly breakdown.


``` r
ny_arrests <- get_arrest_count("NY0112000", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
ny_arrests
#>   geography                                 offense  period count   rate
#> 1 NY0112000 Homer Village Police Department Arrests 01-2019     2  64.52
#> 2 NY0112000 Homer Village Police Department Arrests 02-2019     2  64.52
#> 3 NY0112000 Homer Village Police Department Arrests 03-2019     2  64.52
#> 4 NY0112000                        New York Arrests 01-2019    NA 160.79
#> 5 NY0112000                        New York Arrests 02-2019    NA 150.39
#> 6 NY0112000                        New York Arrests 03-2019    NA 176.87
#> 7 NY0112000                   United States Arrests 01-2019    NA 251.34
#> 8 NY0112000                   United States Arrests 02-2019    NA 236.27
#> 9 NY0112000                   United States Arrests 03-2019    NA 269.73
```


``` r
get_arrest_count("NY0112000", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019", offense = "Robbery")
#>   geography offense period count rate
#> 1 NY0112000 Robbery   <NA>     0   NA
```

`get_arrest_demographics()` returns arrestee sex/race/age breakdowns.

**Limitation:** demographics are only available aggregated across *all*
offenses -- the CDE API does not break demographics down by offense.
`get_arrest_demographics_all()` (a name kept for backward compatibility)
always warns and ignores any offense you pass it, falling back to
`offense = "all"`.


``` r
wa_arrest_demographics <- get_arrest_demographics(state_abb = "WA", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
head(wa_arrest_demographics)
#>   geography offense period demographic_type demographic_value count
#> 1        WA     all   <NA>     Arrestee Sex              Male 29698
#> 2        WA     all   <NA>     Arrestee Sex            Female 11208
#> 3        WA     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race             Asian  1403
#> 4        WA     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race             White 30517
#> 5        WA     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race           Unknown  1201
#> 6        WA     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race          Multiple     0
```

## NIBRS

`get_nibrs_victim()`, `get_nibrs_offender()`, and `get_nibrs_offense()` wrap
`nibrs/{level}/{offense}?type=totals`, returning victim, offender, and
offense-characteristic demographic breakdowns.


``` r
get_nibrs_victim("CA0010900", offense = "robbery", variable = "race")
```

As of this package version, the live NIBRS demographic-detail endpoint
returns no data for any agency, offense, or date range -- this is a known,
tracked upstream issue
(<https://gitea.civilytics.org/Civilytics/fbi_cde/issues/33>), not a bug in
this package. Calling these functions today will emit a message saying so
and return a 0-row data frame; the chunk above is not evaluated in this
vignette for that reason. Use `list_nibrs_offenses()`,
`list_nibrs_victim_variables()`, `list_nibrs_offender_variables()`, and
`list_nibrs_offense_variables()` to see the valid `offense`/`variable`
arguments once the endpoint is working again.

## Supplemental Homicide Reports (SHR)

`get_shr()` wraps `shr/{level}` for expanded homicide data at the agency,
state, or national level.


``` r
fl_shr <- get_shr(ori = "FL0010100", from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
head(fl_shr)
#>   geography  period count
#> 1 FL0010100 01-2019     0
#> 2 FL0010100 02-2019     0
#> 3 FL0010100 03-2019     0
#> 4 FL0010100 04-2019     0
#> 5 FL0010100 05-2019     0
#> 6 FL0010100 06-2019     0
```


``` r
ma_shr <- get_shr(state_abb = "MA", from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
head(ma_shr)
#>   geography  period count
#> 1        MA 01-2019    11
#> 2        MA 02-2019    11
#> 3        MA 03-2019     8
#> 4        MA 04-2019     3
#> 5        MA 05-2019    14
#> 6        MA 06-2019    14
```


``` r
national_shr <- get_shr(from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
head(national_shr)
#>   geography  period count
#> 1        US 01-2019  1192
#> 2        US 02-2019  1065
#> 3        US 03-2019  1156
#> 4        US 04-2019  1139
#> 5        US 05-2019  1315
#> 6        US 06-2019  1306
```

## Police Employment

`get_police_employment()` wraps `pe/{level}`, using 4-digit years rather than
`MM-YYYY`.


``` r
oakland_pe <- get_police_employment("CA0010900", from = "2018", to = "2020")
oakland_pe
#>   year male_officers female_officers male_civilians female_civilians       ori
#> 1 2018           633              98             60              219 CA0010900
#> 2 2019           636             104             63              220 CA0010900
#> 3 2020           632             108             83              233 CA0010900
#>   male_total female_total civilians_total officers_total employees_total
#> 1        693          317             279            731            1010
#> 2        699          324             283            740            1023
#> 3        715          341             316            740            1056
```

**Limitation:** employee *counts* (`actuals`) are suppressed by the CDE API
above the agency level -- state and national queries only return `rates`
upstream, so `get_police_employment()` correctly returns 0 rows for them:


``` r
texas_pe <- get_police_employment(state_abb = "TX", from = "2018", to = "2020")
nrow(texas_pe)
#> [1] 0
```

## NIBRS Participation

`get_agency_participation()`, `get_state_participation()`, and
`get_region_participation()` report whether agencies currently report to
NIBRS, sourced from the live agency directory. This replaces the retired
year-by-year SRS/NIBRS participation series, which has no live equivalent in
the current API -- these functions report a live NIBRS-reporting snapshot
rather than a historical time series.


``` r
get_agency_participation("NY0112000")
#>         ori                     agency_name agency_type_name state_abbr
#> 1 NY0112000 Homer Village Police Department             City         NY
#>   state_name   county is_nibrs nibrs_start_date
#> 1   New York CORTLAND     TRUE       2021-05-01
```


``` r
get_state_participation("WA")
#>   state_abbr total_agencies nibrs_agencies participation_rate
#> 1         WA            270            270                  1
```


``` r
get_region_participation("South")
#>   region total_agencies nibrs_agencies participation_rate
#> 1  South           8097           7059          0.8718044
```

## LEOKA

`get_leoka()` and `get_leoka_monthly()` wrap `leoka/ytd` and `leoka/monthly`,
reporting on law enforcement officers killed or assaulted. These are
**national only** -- the live endpoint ignores state/agency query
parameters -- and data is only available from 2020 onward.


``` r
leoka <- get_leoka(2020, 2021)
leoka
#>   year month total_officers total_incidents total_officers_dod
#> 1 2020    NA             46              44                  2
#> 2 2021    NA             73              68                  4
#>   total_officers_doi total_incidents_dod total_incidents_doi
#> 1                 44                   2                  42
#> 2                 69                   4                  64
```


``` r
get_leoka_monthly(2020, 1)
#>   year month total_officers total_incidents total_officers_dod
#> 1 2020     1              4               3                  0
#>   total_officers_doi total_incidents_dod total_incidents_doi
#> 1                  4                   0                   3
```
